claims.text: Binder jetting followed by debinding and isothermal sintering will significantly reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Binder-jetted and sintered AlCrFeNiSi components will have improved mechanical properties relative to components produced by conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Preparing AlCrFeNiSi powder under an inert atmosphere minimizes pre-oxidation and maintains high chemical purity.
The proposed intervention replaces laser- or electron-beam melting with ambient-temperature binder jetting followed by debinding and isothermal sintering.
Debinding at moderate temperature can remove the binder without inducing significant thermal gradients.
A sintering window of 1100–1300 K is likely to provide full interparticle diffusion in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature features on the order of 100 µm.
Sintered additively manufactured alloy structures can be mechanically tested at ambient and cryogenic temperatures.
Phased thermal input minimizes steep temperature gradients.
Isothermal sintering enables full interdiffusion and can produce a structurally homogeneous alloy with low residual stress.
Low-thermal-load binder jetting avoids the rapid local heating and cooling associated with beam-based additive manufacturing.
Rapid local heating and cooling induce residual stress and microstructural irregularities.
Isothermal sintering activates diffusion across particle boundaries and promotes alloy homogenization.
Defect healing and phase homogenization enhance mechanical properties.
Binder-jetted and sintered AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit a more homogeneous microstructure and superior strength–ductility performance than high-thermal-load AM controls.
High-energy laser or electron-beam additive manufacturing produces steep thermal gradients that lead to high residual stress, microsegregation, and degraded mechanical properties.
Processing outside the stated sintering-temperature window or with inadequate oxygen control may negate the proposed benefits.
